descs.t: Tucker Carlson claims the Trump administration may be within days of a nuclear strike on Iran, under pressure from Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. Axios separately reports that Netanyahu is pressing Trump to strike right after Tuesday's midterm elections. We go through what Carlson claimed, what the reports say, and how his critics answer him.

Tucker Carlson says a US nuclear strike on Iran could be days away, and he names Netanyahu as the one pushing for it. Critics like Laura Loomer call it a hoax timed for the midterms, while analysts point to the B61-11, the only US nuclear bomb built to burrow, and sites like Pickaxe Mountain. We weigh the claim against the reporting.

Tucker Carlson is warning Americans of a nuclear strike on Iran, two days before the midterms. The regime keeps its enriched uranium buried deep under a mountain, and that is the reason this question exists at all. We take apart the claim, the timing and who it really serves.

intro.plain: Tucker Carlson says the Trump administration may be within days of a nuclear strike on Iran, and he says Netanyahu is pushing for it. Axios reports Netanyahu wants a strike right after Tuesday's midterms. Laura Loomer calls Tucker's claim a hoax. So let's look at what is actually reported. Chat, do you believe Tucker on this one, yes or no?
intro.mid: Two days before the midterms, Tucker Carlson says a US nuclear strike on Iran could be days away, with Netanyahu pushing for it. Axios says Netanyahu wants a strike after Tuesday. Is this a real leak or a hoax timed for the vote? Chat, tell me: what is Tucker really after here?
intro.bold: Tucker Carlson wants you scared. He says Trump could order a nuclear strike on Iran within days, and he blames Netanyahu. Meanwhile the regime keeps its enriched uranium buried under a mountain. Who should Americans really be afraid of here? Chat, is the danger the strike, or the regime's uranium?

hook.plain: Tucker Carlson says a US nuclear strike on Iran may be days away, and that Netanyahu is pushing for it. Here is what he claimed and what the reporting shows.
hook.mid: Two days before the midterms, Tucker Carlson warns of a nuclear strike on Iran. Real leak, or a hoax with perfect timing? Let's check it against the reports.
hook.bold: The B61-11 is the only US nuclear bomb built to burrow. Tucker Carlson says it is about to be used on Iran. Here is who that fear really serves.

descs.t: Poland's Constitutional Tribunal is at the center of a fight between Prime Minister Donald Tusk and President Karol Nawrocki, after police surrounded the court and its president was suspended. The EU says Poland's parliament must have the right to appoint new judges, while Nawrocki says he will never let Brussels take powers from Poland. We walk through what happened and what each side claims.

Donald Tusk's critics call the move on Poland's Constitutional Tribunal a coup, and some of Nawrocki's critics say the coup is his. Marine Le Pen raised the alarm, and the EU backed parliament's right to appoint judges. We separate the claims from what is reported.

A Polish father confronts his son, a police officer, on the line outside the Constitutional Tribunal, and the video spreads fast. Poland is split over who controls its top court, and propaganda networks are working to widen that split. We look at the standoff, the claims on both sides, and who gains from a divided Poland.

intro.plain: Poland is in a fight over its top court. Police surrounded the Constitutional Tribunal, its president was suspended, and Donald Tusk's critics are calling it a coup. President Karol Nawrocki says he will never let Brussels take Poland's powers, and the EU backs parliament's right to appoint judges. Let's go through what is reported. Chat, who do you think is right here?
intro.mid: In Poland, both sides are using the word coup. Tusk's critics say he seized the Constitutional Tribunal. Some of Nawrocki's critics say the coup is his. The EU has taken parliament's side on appointing judges. Chat, is this a coup, or a messy fight over a court?
intro.bold: A father in Warsaw stands in front of his own son, a police officer guarding Poland's top court, and tells him he did not raise him this way. That is how deep this split goes, and propaganda networks are pouring fuel on it. Chat, who wins if Poland keeps fighting itself?

hook.plain: Police surrounded Poland's Constitutional Tribunal and its president was suspended. Tusk's critics call it a coup. Here is what happened and what each side claims.

descs.t: Texas early voting closed with 7,705,786 votes, about 74.1% of projected final turnout, ahead of Tuesday's Senate race between Republican Ken Paxton and Democrat James Talarico. Recent polls range from Paxton ahead by 0.6 to Talarico ahead by 4. We go through the numbers and what they can and cannot tell us.

With 7.7 million early votes in, Texas heads into Tuesday with a Senate race the polls cannot agree on: Trafalgar has Ken Paxton up 0.6, YouGov has James Talarico up 4. The governor's race between Greg Abbott and Gina Hinojosa also looks close in some polls. We look at where Texas really stands.

Texas turned out in near presidential numbers before Election Day, and Ken Paxton's Senate race against James Talarico is within a point in one final poll. Democrats talk about flipping the state, Republicans say Latino men are sticking with Trump. We break down the early vote and what it means for Tuesday.

intro.plain: Texas early voting is done: 7,705,786 votes, about 74.1% of the projected turnout. The Senate race is Ken Paxton against James Talarico, and the final polls disagree, from Paxton up 0.6 to Talarico up 4. Chat, if you are in Texas, did you vote early, and how does it feel on the ground?
intro.mid: Texas just finished early voting with 7.7 million ballots. One final poll has Ken Paxton ahead by 0.6, another has James Talarico ahead by 4. The governor's race may be close too. That is not the Texas we are used to. Chat, is this the year Texas surprises everyone, or is it hype?
intro.bold: Texas turned out in force: 7.7 million early votes, and Ken Paxton's Senate race is within a point in one final poll. Democrats think they can flip it, Republicans say the base is holding. Two days out, Texas is a real fight. So chat, call it now: Paxton or Talarico?

descs.t: Democratic Rep. Haley Stevens has endorsed Republican Mike Rogers over Democrat Abdul El-Sayed in Michigan's Senate race, days before Tuesday's vote. Other Michigan Democrats, among them former Detroit Congressman Hansen Clarke, have also crossed over, according to reports. We walk through what each candidate says and how the endorsement is shaking up the race.

Haley Stevens, who lost the Democratic primary to Abdul El-Sayed, is now backing Republican Mike Rogers for Michigan's Senate seat, and Democrats are furious. Posts citing the Washington Post say the state party has thrown her out, while El-Sayed's campaign says it raised $1.2 million in four hours after the news. We look at why she did it and what it could mean on Tuesday.

The Michigan Senate race just got blown open: Democrat Haley Stevens crossed the aisle to endorse Republican Mike Rogers over Abdul El-Sayed, and more Michigan Democrats have followed. Trump says he would love to have her, Schumer reportedly calls it despicable, and El-Sayed's camp says the money is pouring in. We break down who gains, who loses, and whether it changes the result.

intro.plain: Big news out of Michigan before Tuesday's vote. Democratic Rep. Haley Stevens, who lost the primary to Abdul El-Sayed, has endorsed Republican Mike Rogers for the Senate. A few other Michigan Democrats have crossed over too. So today we look at what each candidate stands for and why this matters. Chat, tell me: does an endorsement like this actually move votes, or just headlines?
intro.mid: Michigan's Senate race just turned upside down. Haley Stevens, a Democrat, endorsed Republican Mike Rogers over her own party's nominee, Abdul El-Sayed. Reports say the state party threw her out, and El-Sayed's campaign says it raised $1.2 million in four hours afterward. So who comes out ahead? Chat, I want to know: is Stevens a traitor to her party, or did she just say what others think?
intro.bold: Days before the vote, a Democrat just handed Michigan's Senate race a grenade. Haley Stevens endorsed Republican Mike Rogers over Abdul El-Sayed, other Democrats followed, and her party is in open revolt. Trump says he'd love to have her. El-Sayed's camp says money is flooding in. Chat, call it now: does this sink El-Sayed on Tuesday, or does it backfire on Rogers?

hook.plain: A Michigan Democrat has endorsed the Republican for Senate, days before the vote. Here is who Haley Stevens backed, why she says she did it, and where the race stands.
hook.mid: Haley Stevens lost the primary to Abdul El-Sayed. Now she is backing his Republican opponent, and Democrats are furious. Here is what it means for Michigan on Tuesday.
